newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB a hold, EPS upgraded - Generale Bank.
newsitem.headline: UCB a hold, EPS upgraded - Generale Bank.

text.p: Belgium's Generale Bank said on Wednesday it recommended investors hold on to shares in Belgian chemical and drugs group UCB despite a slight upward revision of forecast 1996 earnings per share (EPS).

"Our 'hold' recommendation is based on the anticipation of a small positive surprise at the release of 1996 results at the end of January and the expected green light for Zyrtec in Japan by the middle of the year," the bank said in a research note.
At an estimated price/earnings ratio of 33 in 1996 and 28 in 1997 "the share seems more than fully valued," the bank added, basing its comments on a share price of 90,200 francs.
It forecast EPS up by two percent for 1996 to 2,722 francs following a better-than-expected performance of the chemical sector during the second half of the year.
A strong dollar and a slight increase in estimated 1996 U.S. sales of UCB's star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec to $125 million from $120 million also helped.

By 1045 GMT UCB was up 0.83 percent at 90,950 francs after rising 4.4 percent on Tuesday, helped by a recent proposal by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to withdraw approval of the anti-allergy drug Seldane by UCB's rival Hoechst because of potential side effects.

"Note, however, that these warnings from the FDA on Seldane are not new and explain the launch in September 1996 by Hoechst of a new anti-allergy drug, Allegra, with fewer side effects," the bank said. "The reaction in the (UCB) share price seems overdone."
